finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> endpoint returns the full invoice record, including the customer field, to any caller with no authentication or ownership check. Severity HIGH; may be CRITICAL if IDs are guessable, MEDIUM if IDs are random 128-bit capability tokens.
finding.source: Anonymous network request; inv_id path parameter (invoices.py:7)

trace.note: get_invoice(inv_id) has no g.user or permission check
INVOICES.get(inv_id) or abort(404) is a lookup only
return jsonify(inv) returns the record to any caller

finding.guards_checked: No before_request hook, decorator, or auth check in this file; no ownership comparison; sibling /my/invoice/<inv_id> (invoices.py:13-18) enforces inv["customer"] != g.user["id"], so the unprotected route looks like an oversight. Auth middleware outside the repository could still apply, and ID format is unknown. Validation tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:7-10 has no auth decorator, no before_request hook, and no ownership check. The only guard is the 404 lookup at invoices.py:9, which is not an authorization check. Nothing else in the directory (only invoices.py and .claude/skills docs) adds middleware. The sibling route at invoices.py:16-17 does enforce ownership, so the gap is on this route only.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: /invoice/<inv_id> at invoices.py:7 returns jsonify(inv) at invoices.py:10 with no authentication or ownership check, so an anonymous caller can read any invoice whose ID they know or can guess. Severity is unresolved because the ID format is not visible in the repo (the candidate's HIGH/CRITICAL/MEDIUM range is correct to hedge), and out-of-repo middleware could not be ruled out.
